title: Pascal's Triangle II
statement:
Pascal's triangle is built row by row. Its top row, row 0, is just `[1]`. Each later row has one more entry than the row above it: its first and last entries are `1`, and every entry in between equals the sum of the two entries of the previous row that sit just above it (the one at the same position and the one to its left).

Return row number `rowIndex` (counting from 0) as a list of its entries from left to right.
notes:
## Intuition

Building the whole triangle as a list of rows works but keeps O(n²) numbers around. Each row depends only on the row above it, so one list can be turned into the next row in place. The trick is the direction: if we update from right to left, `row[j - 1]` still holds the old value when `row[j]` needs it.

## Approach

1. Start with `row = [1]`, which is row 0.
2. For each new row `i` from 1 to `rowIndex`, append a `1` for the new last entry.
3. Walk `j` from `i - 1` down to `1` and set `row[j] += row[j - 1]`: the old `row[j]` is the entry above, and the untouched `row[j - 1]` is the entry above and to the left.
4. The first entry stays `1`. After the last pass, `row` is the answer.

## Example 1, step by step

`rowIndex = 3`. Start with `[1]`.
- `i = 1`: push gives `[1, 1]`; the inner loop does nothing.
- `i = 2`: push gives `[1, 1, 1]`; `j = 1` makes `row[1] = 1 + 1 = 2`, so `[1, 2, 1]`.
- `i = 3`: push gives `[1, 2, 1, 1]`; `j = 2` makes `row[2] = 1 + 2 = 3`, then `j = 1` makes `row[1] = 2 + 1 = 3`, so `[1, 3, 3, 1]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²) for `n = rowIndex`: row `i` needs about `i` additions.
- Space: O(n): only the one row is stored.

## Pitfalls

- Updating left to right would add an already-updated neighbour: row 3 would come out as `[1, 3, 4, 1]`.
- Row `rowIndex` has `rowIndex + 1` entries; rows are counted from 0.
- The largest entry for `rowIndex = 33` is about 1.17 billion, which still fits a 32-bit signed integer; computing `C(n, k)` from factorials would overflow without big integers.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `row` | the current row, rewritten in place into the next one |
| `i` | index of the row being built |
| `j` | position being updated, moving right to left |

narration.2: Row 0 of the triangle is a single 1.
narration.4: Build rows 1 through rowIndex, one at a time, in the same list.
narration.5: Each new row is one longer and always ends with a 1.
narration.6: Walk the inner positions from right to left so the left neighbour is still the old value.
narration.7: New entry = the entry above it plus the entry above and to the left.
narration.10: After the last pass the list holds row rowIndex.
